# Workflow and work plan

Mermaid diagrams are written as text in `{mermaid}` cells, so they can be versioned and reviewed like the rest of the report. Cell options use the `%%|` prefix, and a `fig-` label makes them cross-referenceable.

## Analysis workflow

@fig-workflow summarises the reporting pipeline used in this template.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-workflow
%%| fig-cap: "Analysis and reporting workflow."
%%| fig-width: 6.2
flowchart LR
  A[Raw data] --> B[Processing<br/>Python / R]
  B --> C{Validated?}
  C -- yes --> D[Figures and tables]
  C -- no --> B
  D --> E[Quarto report]
  E --> F[PDF via Typst]
  E --> G[HTML]
```

## Work plan

@fig-gantt shows a simple project schedule. Mermaid Gantt charts suit plans with up to about fifteen tasks; for larger schedules, build the chart in Python so it can follow the report palette exactly.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-gantt
%%| fig-cap: "Indicative project work plan."
%%| fig-width: 6.5
gantt
  dateFormat  YYYY-MM-DD
  axisFormat  %b %Y
  section WP1 Modelling
    Literature review       :done,   t1, 2026-01-01, 60d
    Model development       :active, t2, after t1, 90d
  section WP2 Experiments
    Test rig set-up         :        t3, 2026-03-01, 75d
    Measurement campaign    :        t4, after t3, 60d
  section WP3 Reporting
    Interim report          :milestone, m1, 2026-06-30, 0d
    Final deliverable       :        t5, after t4, 45d
```
